pages.text: Hit a $(thing)wet$() target with a $(thing)Fire$() attack worth at least $(thing)50 Fire power$() and the water flash-boils: a $(thing)High-Heat Steam Cloud$() erupts from the victim, and the wetness is consumed to fuel it.$(br2)Fire power is your total Fire Enhancement in points. 50 points is 10 levels across your armour.

pages.title: Inside the cloud
pages.text: $(li)$(thing)1 damage per second$(), increased by 20% per cloud level.$(br2)$(li)Higher levels come from wetter victims - 5 levels of Wetness makes a level 5 cloud: 2 damage per second, radius 6.$(li)Nature and Frost-tempered victims take $(thing)50% more$() scalding.$(li)Everybody inside is $(thing)blinded$() and mobs panic and forget their target.$(li)It strips Wetness, Frostbite and Freeze from anyone inside.$(br2)Fire Resistance or 80 Fire Resistance points makes you immune.

pages.title: Drying yourself off
pages.text: The same reaction happens to $(l)you$(). If you are wet and land a Fire attack, you dry out instantly - each $(thing)20 Fire power$() burns off one level of Wetness.$(br2)That attack deals $(thing)30% less$() damage, and a $(thing)Low-Heat Steam Cloud$() forms at your feet. Attacking while soaked is self-defence, not a free win.

pages.title: Low-Heat Steam
pages.text: $(#8cf)Low-Heat Steam Clouds$() are cold mist, not scalding steam. They appear whenever water is evaporated without much heat:$(br2)$(li)Drying yourself off.$(li)Melted Freeze.$(li)$(thing)Thermal Shock$().$(br2)Inside one you take no damage, but you are blinded and the mist $(thing)condenses onto you$(), adding Wetness level by level until you are soaked again. Standing in your own steam re-soaks you.

pages.title: Thermal Shock
pages.text: Scorched targets cannot be extinguished by water. Jumping into a lake while on fire instead triggers a $(thing)Thermal Shock$():$(br2)$(li)Scalding steam explodes around you.$(li)$(thing)50% of all the remaining burn damage$() is dealt at once.$(li)A Low-Heat Steam Cloud is left behind, and the water block you entered is boiled away.$(br2)Water is faster than burning, but it is not safer.
